values.value: every signal that reaches an RP2354B pin is at 3.3 V logic. GPIO0 to 39 are rated to 5.5 V while IOVDD is at 3.3 V, and to 3.63 V while IOVDD is at 0 V. A 5 V output that can drive before the 3.3 V rail is up is translated to 3.3 V
values.source: RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29, https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rp2350/rp2350-datasheet.pdf (final URL pip-assets.raspberrypi.com/.../RP-008373-DS-2-rp2350-datasheet.pdf), read 2026-09-28T10:26:39Z. Table 1426 (Pin Types); Table 1427 (GPIO pins); Table 1433 (Absolute maximum ratings). These are Tables 1423, 1424 and 1430 of build 2024-08-08, which IOBoard.md cites
values.refutation_tried: Read build 2025-07-29. Table 1433 gives VPIN_FT −0.5 to 5.5 V at IOVDD = 3.3 V and −0.5 to 3.63 V at IOVDD = 0 V. Table 1427 lists GPIO0 to GPIO39 as Digital IO (FT). Table 1426 says 'very little current' below 3.63 V with IOVDD at 0 V and gives no figure. Figures match. For R13 this binds the bridge ADC's digital lines: they need 3.3 V logic on a 3.3 V digital supply pin, or translation.

values.quantity: ADC-input front end rating while the 3.3 V rail is down
values.value: a front end that drives one of the 8 ADC inputs keeps it within its rating (IOVDD + 0.5 V) while the 3.3 V rail is down and the front end's supply is up
values.source: Research.md:269-272; RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29, read 2026-09-28T10:26:39Z. Table 1433: VPIN (Standard) −0.5 V to IOVDD + 0.5 V. Table 1427: GPIO40_ADC0 to GPIO47_ADC7 are 'Digital IO / Analogue', not FT
values.refutation_tried: Read all 8 rows of Table 1427 and the VPIN row of Table 1433. The rating reads as stated. It binds R13 only if the design drives an RP2354B ADC input, for example an amplifier into the internal ADC. A bridge ADC with a digital interface falls under the IOBoard.md:105 value instead.

questions.question: Which supply gives the 5 V load-cell excitation of F3: the IO board's 5 V rail, which also carries the display's 1.5 A continuous and 2 A peak, or a separate supply for the bridges?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:338 counts the excitation as a load on the 5 V rail. F3 fixes only its voltage. The answer decides three things. First, whether the excitation is the rail itself or a part R13 selects. Second, which analogue supply and reference-input range the bridge ADC must accept. Third, which rail R5 (T3) sizes for the excitation current. P2 cannot qualify the excitation or the ADC's reference input without it.

questions.question: What is the bridge resistance of each of the 3 load cells (the thrust cell and the 2 torque cells), in Ω?
questions.why: Each cell draws 5 V divided by its bridge resistance, and the currents of the cells on one excitation add up. IOBoard.md:338 gives the excitation current as not stated. P2 needs the current to rate the excitation part. R5 (T3) needs it to size the 5 V rail. The load cells are not a part T4 selects, so P4 does not report their draw.

questions.question: What is the rated output of each of the 3 load cells (the thrust cell and the 2 torque cells), in mV/V?
questions.why: Rated output × 5 V excitation gives each channel's full-scale differential input, in mV. That fixes the input range and programmable gain the bridge ADC needs. Neither page states it.

questions.question: What is the rated capacity of each of the 3 load cells (the thrust cell and the 2 torque cells), in N?
questions.why: It converts a load step in N into a voltage step at the ADC input: step / capacity × rated output × 5 V. Without it, P2 cannot turn the resolution in N into the noise-free resolution in µV a part must reach. Neither page states it.

questions.question: What thrust range, in N, and what torque range, in N·m, must the bench measure, each from its largest negative to its largest positive value?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:495 gives the ranges as not stated and assigns them to R13. They set how much of each cell's full-scale output the ADC input spans. They also set whether each channel reads both signs: reverse thrust, and both directions of rotation.

questions.question: What is the smallest load change, in N, that each load cell's channel must resolve (the thrust cell and each torque cell), at the output rate asked for the load-cell channels?
questions.why: With the rated capacity and the rated output, it gives the step at the ADC input in µV. That is the noise-free resolution the bridge ADC must reach at its data rate. Neither page states a resolution for thrust or torque.

questions.question: What accuracy must each load-cell channel hold, in % of the cell's rated output, counting the bridge ADC's and the excitation's gain and offset errors and their drift with temperature?
questions.why: It bounds the gain error, offset, nonlinearity and drift the ADC may have. It also bounds the excitation's drift if the measurement is not ratiometric. Neither page states an accuracy for thrust or torque.

questions.question: At what output rate must each of the 3 load-cell channels be read, in samples per second per channel?
questions.why: A multiplexed converter splits its data rate across the channels and must settle after each switch. So the rate per channel decides between one multiplexed converter and one converter per channel, and sets the digital filter. The 20 ms sampling at IOBoard.md:431 covers the BENCH numbers, which carry no thrust or torque, so it does not set this rate.

questions.question: How far apart in time, in ms, may the readings of the 2 torque cells, and of the thrust cell, be taken? May one multiplexed converter read them in turn, or must they be converted at the same instant?
questions.why: F3 takes torque from 2 cells. The allowed time between readings decides whether the 3 channels can share one multiplexed converter or need simultaneous conversion. That choice fixes the part and its placements per board, and so the need in the stock gate of sourcing rule 4.

questions.question: Does each load cell connect with 4 wires (excitation and signal) or with 6 wires (excitation, signal and sense leads)?
questions.why: A 6-wire cell's sense leads go to the ADC's reference input. The part then needs a differential reference input for each sensed cell, or the cells share one excitation and one pair of sense leads. P2 cannot count the reference inputs and channels a part needs without this. F3 gives only the channels and the excitation.
